subject: Follow-up: DPA/SCC selection, controller role confirmation & next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@finacorp.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo notes and GDPR routing asks

Hi Samantha — great to meet you and the security team earlier. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Call highlights:
- Finacorp confirmed the integration pattern and sample PII flows (payment tokenization + customer identifiers).
- Primary ask: written DPA and confirmation of which SCC module Redwood will adopt. You mentioned preference for an SCC module that supports controller-to-processor relationships.
- Other asks: SOC 2 Type II evidence, subprocessors list, and clarity on retention/deletion for cached tokens and logs.

Our current position / what we can provide immediately:
- Redwood acts as a processor for the flows discussed (we do not determine purpose/means). We will sign a DPA reflecting processor responsibilities.
- Recommended SCC module: Module 2 (controller-to-processor with standard SCC clauses) — this maps cleanly to typical SaaS use cases and Finacorp's needs, but happy to adjust if your legal team prefers Module 3 variants.
- Attached: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025.pdf and a copy of our standard Redwood_DPA_Template_v1.docx to speed review.

Proposed next steps and owners:
1) We send the DPA via DocuSign for signature (Jordan / Legal) — target: within 3 business days.
2) Security kickoff: begin vendor questionnaire (we can intake your XLS and assign to Security) — target: questionnaire launched by EOD tomorrow.
3) Provide subprocessors list and retention specifics (Marcus owning) — Marcus will attach the current list and describe retention and deletion windows.
4) Confirm whether HIPAA Business Associate Agreement is required beyond the DPA (please confirm).

If you can confirm the SCC module preference and whether Finacorp is the controller for the data types in scope, we will proceed on the timeline above.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0112
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025.pdf, Redwood_DPA_Template_v1.docx
From: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@finacorp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finacorp.com
Date: 2026-10-11T10:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo notes and GDPR routing asks

Jordan — thanks for the recap and the quick turnaround on materials. Short answers from Security/Legal at Finacorp: 

- Finacorp will act as the controller for the data classes we discussed (customer identifiers, payment metadata).
- Preference: SCC Module 2 is our default for SaaS vendors acting as processors; that aligns with our counsel.
- SOC 2: we need the Type II report and the control summary (you attached the Type II; please confirm the date range and whether any exclusions apply).
- Subprocessors: please provide a list with purpose and region.
- Retention: we need to see the retention and deletion approach for cached tokens (we currently require a max retention of 90 days for any cached PII unless otherwise agreed).
- HIPAA: not required for this integration, but we may have future applications that will. Please state whether Redwood supports a BAA.

I've attached our vendor security questionnaire (Finacorp_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx) — please fill the relevant tabs. Procurement will track execution and signature. Timeline: procurement/legal prefer complete intake + DPA signature within two weeks; security would like the questionnaire answers within 5 business days.

Samantha Reed
Head of Security, Finacorp
Samantha.Reed@finacorp.com
Phone: +1 (212) 555-0199

Attachment: Finacorp_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: next moves on Finacorp DPA/SCC request

Looping in quick internal plan so we don't miss deadlines.

- Legal: I'll review the DPA template and prepare the DocuSign envelope. Goal: send to Finacorp within 48 hours.
- Security (Marcus): please extract the subprocessors list and add purpose + hosting region. Also call out any subprocessors that store or cache KV-level data.
- Product Ops: confirm retention defaults for cached tokens and options to configure retention per-customer (we should offer 90-day default and a shorter option if requested).
- BAA: Flag to Prod/Security for input; we need a decision whether Redwood offers BAAs today and what the time-to-sign would be.

I'll own coordination with procurement and will update HubSpot (DEAL-78291) with milestones. Jordan, can you confirm the DocuSign link you want us to use or do you want Legal to create the envelope?

Lauren
Director, Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@finacorp.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo notes and GDPR routing asks

Thanks Samantha — appreciate the clarity. Quick answers and actions from our side: 

1) Controller/Processor: confirmed — Redwood will be the processor for the scoped flows and we will sign a DPA reflecting that role. SCC Module 2 is acceptable to us.

2) SOC 2 evidence: attached is Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025.pdf (coverage period 2025-01-01 through 2025-12-31). No exclusions on the report; control matrix summary available on request.

3) Subprocessors: attached Redwood_Subprocessor_List_2026.txt with vendor name, purpose, and region. Marcus to follow up if you need full contracts.

4) Retention: default retention for ephemeral caches is 90 days; logs kept for up to 365 days with redaction of PII where possible. We can offer a shorter retention for your environment; please tell us target if 90 days is a blocker.

5) BAA: Redwood supports HIPAA use cases via a separate BAA offering; I'll have Security confirm timeline but preliminary estimate is a 7-10 business day review for a standard BAA addendum.

6) DocuSign: sending DPA via DocuSign now — put the HubSpot link here for your team: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/78291 and DocuSign envelope: https://www.docusign.com/link/12345678

7) Questionnaire: we will intake your XLS into our OneTrust/Intake tracker and assign a security owner. Here is the intake link we will use to start the questionnaire: https://onetrust.example.com/finacorp/questionnaire/98765

Proposed immediate timeline: DocuSign DPA sent today; questionnaire started today; most questionnaire items answered within 3-5 business days; finalize signatures within 10 business days if no redlines. If that works for your procurement cadence we will proceed.

Would you like a short security kickoff call Tuesday at 10am PT to walk the questionnaire and subprocessors list?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_Subprocessor_List_2026.txt
